title: POC scoping: Interop playbook / SDK + OpenAI-compat - EmberCore
summary: Initial POC scoping to define success criteria, benchmark plan, and an integration playbook for EmberCore. Focus on OpenAI-compatible endpoints, SDKs (Python/Node), function calling and structured output validation. Agreed to run three benchmark workloads, provide a test account, and schedule a 1-week follow-up after baseline results.
action_items: Carlos Mendes - create benchmark harness script + load profile (base + 2 spikes) - due 2026-10-26
Anika Rao - draft SDK integration guide (Python + Node) and sample tool-calling example - due 2026-10-25
EmberCore / Evan Brooks - provide representative prompt sets and expected JSON schemas for structured responses - due 2026-10-24
Lydia Park - share security pack (SOC2, pen-test summary), pricing sheet, and ephemeral test creds for Redwood hosted sandbox - due 2026-10-22
Priya Singh - confirm network constraints and whether private VPC deployment will be required for the pilot - due 2026-10-23
next_steps: Redwood to provision sandbox project + API keys (hosted) and send to EmberCore
EmberCore to share workload traces and sample prompts
Schedule benchmark window (3 days) next week and invite platform + SEs
Follow-up call to review baseline numbers on 2026-10-28
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-21
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Lydia Park (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (Redwood), Maya Chen (EmberCore CTO), Evan Brooks (EmberCore Lead ML Eng), Priya Singh (Platform), Raj Patel (Security)

Auto-summary: Quick POC scope to align on success criteria, workload sizing and a benchmark plan. Decide on OpenAI-compat endpoints and SDK examples, plus structured output contract. Action items and due dates captured.

[00:00] Lydia (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro - i'm lydia, i'm the AE on the account, and with me is carlos and anika. we wanted to run through a pragmatic poc plan so you can validate latency, cost, and structured output for your assistant.
[00:22] Maya (EmberCore): thanks lydia, appreciate it. i'll keep it high level — embercore is building a customer support agent that needs to ingest docs, call internal tools, and return structured JSON payloads to our downstream systems.
[00:40] Evan (EmberCore): yep. main success metrics for us are accuracy of the structured output (schema conformance), p95 latency under load, and predictable unit cost. timeline is tight — pilot in 4 weeks if possible.
[01:05] Carlos (Redwood): cool. a practical approach we recommend: three benchmark scenarios — chat short responses (40-80 tokens), long form summarization (400-800 tokens), and tool-invocation flows with a double round trip. we run these on our hosted endpoints first to get baseline numbers.
[01:30] Priya (EmberCore): quick question — are you able to run our tests against an OpenAI-compatible endpoint? our infra expects that API shape because it's easiest to swap later.
[01:45] Anika (Redwood): yes, we expose OpenAI-compatible endpoints and native SDKs. we also have function-calling support that maps to the same semantics — and we can return structured JSON. caveat: enforcing strict schema validation is typically done client-side or via a simple validation layer we can ship as an example.
[02:12] Raj (EmberCore): security stuff — we'll need SOC2 docs, KMS integration for any private deployments, audit logs, and SSO. we might require private VPC for the pilot depending on legal.
[02:30] Lydia (Redwood): we can share our SOC2 report and how KMS integrates for Private. for hosted, we provide encrypted at rest and optional BYOK for dedicated/private. audit logs + per-token tracing is available via the console.
[02:50] Evan: for sizing — our peak concurrent users for the pilot is ~250 active sessions, average 2 calls per minute, with bursts up to 400 concurrent. average response size 60 tokens for chat. summarization path will be lower QPS but heavier tokens.
[03:12] Carlos: ok, that maps to roughly 100-120 rps for chat, and maybe 10-15 rps for summarization. for p95 latency targets, what's your bar?
[03:25] Maya: ideally p95 < 300ms for chat, p95 < 2s for summarization. cost target is under $0.002 per 1k tokens? — that might be optimistic but we need a number to optimize towards.
[03:44] Anika: we'll show model/quantization tradeoffs. on hosted, smaller quantized variants can hit lower cost but sometimes increase latency slightly for long sequences. our optimize tool will recommend profiles per workload.
[04:05] Lydia: about structured output — can you share a canonical JSON schema for the fields you must receive? examples help a lot for test harness generation.
[04:20] Evan: yes, we'll send 20 canonical prompts and expected schemas. also some edge cases where fields are missing.
[04:30] Carlos: perfect. we'll wire up a validator step in the benchmark harness to compute schema conformance (pass/fail), and a quality metric like BLEU or JSON schema diff for structural mismatches.
[04:50] Priya: what about tool calling? we have internal microservices that the agent needs to call (e.g., ticket lookup, customer profile, escalation). we want the model to return a tool call spec and not hallucinate arguments.
[05:05] Anika: we recommend an explicit function schema for each tool. Redwood's function-calling maps to a typed JSON call; we'll include examples that show a tool invocation, then an execution result, then a follow-up prompt. we also support a hard fallback: if schema fails, you can route to a safe default.
[05:35] Raj: auditability — can we capture all tool invocations and responses? we need to reconcile later.
[05:45] Carlos: yes, the call trace and tokenized payloads can be retained in audit logs. retention options are configurable in the console — retention windows and export hooks.
[06:05] Maya: benchmark duration and windows? we prefer a short smoke, then a 48-hour stability run to see regressions over time.
[06:18] Carlos: plan: 1) quick smoke (2 hours) to validate endpoints and scripts, 2) 3-day benchmark for throughput+stability with a 48-hour steady-state window and a 2-hour spike test. we'll produce p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, and schema conformance.
[06:44] Lydia: timeline alignment — embercore needs pilot sign-off and legal OK by mid-november. that gives us roughly 4 weeks. we should schedule the baseline run next week.
[06:58] Evan: one more — do you have SDK examples for streaming responses and partial JSON assembly? our client wants to start rendering partial answers while the model streams.
[07:12] Anika: yes, Node and Python SDKs support streaming and partial commit patterns. for structured output you'll want to either stream JSON chunks or stream plain text and run an eventual aggregator that validates full JSON. we'll provide both patterns.
[07:34] Priya: network egress — if we end up on private, what's the onboarding time?
[07:43] Lydia: Private or dedicated usually needs 2-3 weeks for infra setup plus a security review. hosted sandbox is immediate. given your timeline i'd suggest starting hosted for benchmarks and then plan private/dedicated cutover if legal requires it.
[08:05] Raj: will you support SAML + SCIM for user provisioning in the console?
[08:12] Carlos: yes, SAML SSO + SCIM are supported. we also have RBAC roles and fine-grained project-level permissions.
[08:28] Maya: what about fallback policies — if the primary model is busy do you have automatic fallbacks?
[08:35] Anika: yes, smart routing allows fallback to a compatible variant. the tradeoff is usually cost vs latency vs quality; we'll document recommended policies in the playbook.
[08:50] Evan: curious about token accounting — does the benchmark include both prompt + response tokens?
[08:57] Carlos: yes, our reporting includes prompt tokens, generation tokens, and total tokens per request. cost modelling will use total tokens.
[09:10] Lydia: ok let's align on concrete success criteria now — maya, can you confirm priority order?
[09:18] Maya: 1) structured output conformance >= 98% on canonical prompts, 2) p95 latency for chat < 300ms at target load, 3) error rate < 1%, 4) acceptable cost per 1k tokens we can negotiate after baseline.
[09:38] Carlos: noted. we'll surface an initial baseline doc with numbers and confidence intervals.
[09:50] Priya: can you also include quantized model profiles? some of our infra prefers lower memory footprints.
[09:58] Anika: yes we'll include CPU/GPU memory footprints and throughput curves per quantization level.
[10:12] Maya: perfect. about the SDK contract — we need code samples that show how to call, how to validate schema, and how to do tool calls with idempotency keys.
[10:28] Anika: will do. we'll send a repo link and a small example app that exercises the tool-calling flow.
[10:40] Lydia: last bit — legal/procurement will need pricing and a short run-of-show doc for pilot sign-off. i will attach those to the follow-up email.
[10:52] Evan: are we ok to proceed with hosted sandbox next week?
[10:56] Lydia: yes — we will provision and share creds by friday.
[11:05] Maya: great, thanks everyone.
[11:07] Lydia: thanks — we'll capture the action items and send notes.
[11:12] (call ends)
